originalTitle: US Senate confirms Jay Clayton as intelligence director, after Wyden calls him Trump’s ‘election conspiracy wingman’ – live
summary: Oregon Democrat said Clayton is an unqualified conspiracy theorist before 51-to-47 vote
content: With Volodymyr Zelenskyy watching from the Senate gallery, the US Senate voted 86 to 12 to advance the “Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act”. Zelenskyy had previously urged senators to support the bill before the vote, despite Democratic reservations that the legislation, as written, would give Donald Trump expansive new powers to waive sanctions on Russians and impose tariffs on “countries that purchase Russian-origin crude oil or natural gas or facilitate sanctions evasion”. Aaron Fritschner, an aide to Democratic congressman Don Beyer of Virginia, argued on social media that the legislation in the Senate bill gives the president too much discretion to waive sanctions and impose tariffs. “The bill has a huge new tariff authority with no expiration, delay, or oversight mechanism,” Fritschner wrote before the Senate vote. “The optional sanctions take up most of the text, but the tariffs are the key policy ingredient and more importantly they are the reason why Republicans and especially the president want this bill to pass.” “There is no limitation, the president can decide which countries this bill applies and hit them with a 100% tariff for five years,” he adds. “Historically, tariff provisions required either long investigations in advance, consultation with Congress, or imposed short, limited durations. This one does not.” “Trump has abused every single major tariff authority!” Fritschner notes. “If you give Trump a tariff authority he WILL abuse it. That’s what he does, it’s all he does.” According to Fritschner, Democrats all want to help Ukraine: is significant even if Trump twists it later. The good news is the House passed a much better bill – the Ukraine Support Act.” “The Ukraine Support Act has proactive support for Ukraine, in addition to sanctions on Russia that are written better, and no new tariffs power,” he adds. “If they pass this bill, Senate Dems will be handing Trump new, massive, unchecked tariff powers in the hope that he will use them against Russia, to help Ukraine, and won’t abuse it in ways that raise Americans’ prices or enrich his own family. Does that sound like a good bet to you?” A small group of demonstrators held a press conference Tuesday outside the hotel where Democratic mayors are meeting in Atlanta to raise a protest against Palantir Technologies Inc, surveillance technology and municipal leaders that contract with its partners. “We’re calling on Jacobs Solutions Inc to publicly explain how the strategic partnerships with Palantir Technologies aligns with the values it promotes to cities, public agencies and communities it serves,” said state representative Eric Bell, a Democrat representing part of Clayton County in Atlanta’s southern suburbs. “Municipal leaders are discussing the future of infrastructure, technology, procurement and public trust. Decisions matter. Technology is never neutral. The tools governments choose to purchase and deploy have real consequences on the people.” Representatives from Metropolis Technologies, Flock Security and other technology firms had speaking slots at the conference. The use of technology like aritificial intelligece to “streamline city services, cut costs, and improve resident experiences–and what it takes to implement them responsibly,” was the subject of one panel discussion. Press were not permitted to attend the conference. Jacobs is an engineering and consulting firm with many clients among large, Democratically-controlled cities like New York City, Los Angeles, Nashville, San Jose and Atlanta, often working on large, complex transportation, sanitation and construction projects. Jacobs and Palantir launched a global strategic partnership in March 2022 for data and technology solutions for infrastructure and national-security markets, starting with water infrastructure. The partnership with Palantir “combines Jacobs’ deep domain knowledge with Palantir’s cutting edge Data and AI technology to create value for clients,” according to Jacobs’ website. “The goal is to deliver real-time computing power, actionable data and control on a time horizon measured in weeks, not years.” Palantir has increasingly come under fire from political progressives after ICE issued the company a $30m contract to build “ImmigrationOS,” designed to speed identification and apprehension of people prioritized for removal and to make deportation logistics more efficient. Palantir has also aided immigration enforcement with software tools to provide a predictive model for neighborhoods. “Palantir has faced significant criticism for work supporting immigration enforcement, large scale, government data analysis, and its close association with prominent Trump allies, including co-founder Peter Thiel,” said Robin Biro, a board member of the Latino civic advocacy organiztion GALEO Impact Fund. “And I’m going to give you a quote from him … he says, ‘I no longer believe that freedom and democracy are compatible.’” Biro was quoting from a piece Thiel wrote for the libertarian Cato Institute in 2009. He has since left the United States and reportedly resides in Argentina. “Those concerns have led to governments and public institutions in multiple counties to publicly question whether the company aligns with their values,” Biro said. “Atlanta has always been a city that leads with civil rights and inclusion and respect for individual liberty. We should demand technology partners that earn public confidence not divided before committing tax dollars.” The US Senate voted 51-to-47 to confirm Jay Clayton as director of national intelligence, installing Donald Trump’s pick in the role despite his lack of prior experience with intelligence. chineseTitle: 在怀登称杰伊·克莱顿为特朗普的“选举阴谋僚机”后，美国参议院确认杰伊·克莱顿为情报总监 - 直播
chineseSummary: 俄勒冈州民主党人在 51 比 47 的投票前称克莱顿是一名不合格的阴谋论者
chineseContent: 在弗拉基米尔·泽伦斯基 (Volodymyr Zelenskyy) 参议院旁听席的注视下，美国参议院以 86 比 12 的投票结果通过了《林赛·格雷厄姆制裁俄罗斯和伊朗法案》。泽连斯基此前曾敦促参议员在投票前支持该法案，尽管民主党对此持保留态度，认为该法案将赋予唐纳德·特朗普广泛的新权力，以免除对俄罗斯人的制裁，并对“购买俄罗斯原产原油或天然气或协助逃避制裁的国家”征收关税。弗吉尼亚州民主党众议员唐·拜尔的助手亚伦·弗里奇纳在社交媒体上辩称，参议院法案中的立法赋予总统太多的自由裁量权，可以免除制裁和征收关税。弗里奇纳在参议院投票前写道：“该法案拥有一个巨大的新关税授权，没有到期、延迟或监督机制。” “选择性制裁占据了文本的大部分内容，但关税是关键的政策成分，更重要的是，它们是共和党人，尤其是总统希望该法案通过的原因。” “没有任何限制，总统可以决定该法案适用于哪些国家，并在五年内对它们征收 100% 的关税，”他补充道。 “从历史上看，关税条款要么需要提前进行长期调查，与国会协商，要么施加短期、有限的期限。而这一条款则不需要。” “特朗普滥用了每一个主要关税权力！”弗里施纳指出。 “如果你给特朗普关税权力，他就会滥用它。这就是他所做的，这就是他所做的一切。”弗里奇纳表示，民主党人都想帮助乌克兰：即使特朗普后来扭曲了这一点，这也很重要。好消息是众议院通过了一项更好的法案——《乌克兰支持法案》。” “乌克兰支持法案除了制裁乌克兰外，还积极支持乌克兰
